PullRequest.Title: agentHost: stop canvas extensions that outlive their folder's trust
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #343771.

## What and why

#343771 launches a project canvas extension (`.github/extensions/<name>/extension.mjs`) only from a folder that VS Code Workspace Trust covers, and stops the extension when that trust is revoked. Its Known limitations list three ways an extension already running could survive the folder losing trust. They were left out of #343771 to keep it reviewable. This PR closes them:

1. **Borrowed from another chat's folder.** Launch requests name no session, and the runtime discovers project extensions at a chat's git root. So chat B can run an extension whose module is in chat A's folder, for example through a link. The policy dropped its record of that launch once no open chat admitted A's folder, so after A closed, revoking A's trust left B's extension running.
2. **An exemption ends.** A quick chat's scratch folder and a host-created worktree are exempt from workspace trust only while their own session admits them. When that session closed, nothing re-checked launches under the exemption, because workspace trust itself didn't change. Likewise, a refused launch wasn't retried when an exemption started.
3. **A reload fails.** After a revocation, a failed reload was only logged. Nothing confirmed that the extension stopped, and nothing retried.

A fourth commit, from review, closes a hole in the confirmation of gap 3. An extension the runtime lists with a source or status this host doesn't know no longer counts as stopped.

Each commit's tests fail on the code before it, and each gap that the UI can drive was reproduced in Code OSS before the fix (see How to test).

## Review guide

Four commits, each building and passing its tests. Reviewing commit by commit is recommended.

### 1. `agentHost: keep revoking canvas extensions a chat runs from another chat's folder` (+218/-52)

In `copilotProjectExtensionLaunchPolicy.ts`, a launch record now keeps the folder the runtime discovered the extension in: the canonical repository root, which can be above a chat's folders. The record is dropped only once no open chat lies in that folder (`_mayRunFrom`). A record without a discovery root is never dropped. The real-runtime test in `copilotMockLlm.integrationTest.ts` covers the cross-chat case with a pid launch log.

### 2. `agentHost: treat canvas trust exemptions ending or starting as trust changes` (+219/-14)

The policy now treats an exemption ending under an allowed launch as a contraction (the same path as revoked trust), and an exemption starting under a refused launch as an expansion (`_noteExemptionChange`). So the borrowing chat stops the extension when the exemption ends, and retries it when the exemption returns. A launch decision that is still resolving trusted folders is re-evaluated when an exemption changes. `copilotAgent.ts` schedules the same reconciliation pass as for workspace trust changes, except while the agent shuts down, and initializing sessions catch up through the same trust counters.

### 3. `agentHost: confirm canvas trust revocations stopped, and restart sessions that can't` (+399/-35)

`CopilotAgentSession` now confirms, by process, that the extensions it ran under revoked trust stopped. None of their pids may still run in a complete extension inventory (`_stopRevokedProjectExtensions`, `_settledRuntimeExtensions`). A same-named extension that trust still covers relaunches under a new pid, which passes. The session retries the reload once before giving up.

- A session that still can't confirm is restarted (`_restartSessionAfterUnconfirmedRevocation`) once it is idle, as after telemetry revocation, or before its next send or control operation, such as opening a canvas or starting an MCP server. Those control operations don't wait for background subagents, the same as after telemetry revocation. Disconnecting a session stops the extensions it ran.
- During initialization the failure stays fatal. A session that already registered is stopped before its caller can use it.
- A session that retires or moves to a new runtime before confirming leaves the revocation to the old runtime's teardown, which disconnects it.

Worth scrutinizing: the idle restart reuses the telemetry-revocation path (`_disposeSessionWhenIdle`), and `isCurrent` in `_settledRuntimeExtensions` stops a confirmation from acting on a successor's runtime.

### 4. `agentHost: treat canvas extension rows with an unknown source or status as unreadable` (+14/-1)

From review. `_listRuntimeExtensions` dropped a row with an unsupported source and mapped an unsupported status to `unknown`, yet still reported the inventory as complete. So a revoked pid listed in such a row passed commit 3's confirmation after a failed reload. Before the reload, a revoked extension listed with an unknown status wasn't counted as running, so it was never reloaded. Both kinds of row now make the inventory incomplete, as a malformed row already did. Revocation then reloads, and restarts the session if a row still can't be read. The listing clients see, `listExtensions()`, is unchanged.

The bundled SDK's types list only sources and statuses this host maps, so this takes a runtime newer than the host, set with the experimental `chat.agentHost.copilot.runtimePath` setting. With such a runtime, any revocation restarts a canvas session that keeps listing a row this host can't read, as a session listing a malformed row already did.

## How to test

Unit and integration tests ran from the branch with `COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS` unset. Agent shells set it, and an inherited `DYNAMIC_AUTO_TIERS` fails an unrelated `CopilotAgent` tiers test.

**On the current base** (`main` at `f9888d5ae28`, `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` `2.0.2-unstable.45286541461.g05667ac` with runtime `1.0.114-unstable`, Node 24.22.1):

| Commit | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| each | `pnpm run typecheck-client`, and `pnpm run oxlint` on the commit's changed files | passed |
| each | `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` | passed |
| each | `./scripts/test.sh --run` for `copilotProjectExtensionLaunchPolicy`, `copilotAgent`, `copilotAgentSession` and `copilotSessionLauncher` (`.test.ts`, under `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/`) | 3,210, 3,213, 3,217, and 3,217 passing for commits 1, 2, 3, and 4, with 1 pending each. Commit 4 adds rows to an existing table test. |
| 4 (tip) | `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run` for `providerIntegration/copilotMockLlm` (10), `providerIntegration/copilotNativeExtensions` (3), `providerIntegration/copilotExtensionEnvConsent` (3), `copilotSdkCanvas` (5) and `e2e/providers/copilotManagedSettingsAgentHostE2E` (15) (`.integrationTest.ts`, under `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/`) | 36 passing |

Each commit's new tests fail on the code before it:

- **Gap 1:** "keeps revoking extensions chats still run from folders whose own chats closed" (policy) returns no revoked launches. The real-runtime test "stops a project canvas extension a chat runs from another chat's folder when that folder loses trust after its chat closed" finds the extension's pid still alive.
- **Gap 2:** "re-evaluates a pending launch decision when an exemption starts while trusted folders resolve" refuses the launch (`allowed: false`). Before this commit the policy has no signal for an exemption starting or ending, so "treats a scratch folder or worktree exemption starting or ending under borrowed launches as a trust change" and "reconciles project extensions when an exemption under a launch starts or ends, except while shutting down" (`CopilotAgent`) fail on the missing `onDidChangeExemptions` rather than on a wrong result. The Code OSS run below shows the behavior that follows.
- **Gap 3:** all four new `CopilotAgent` tests fail on commit 2's source, with `CopilotProjectExtensionRevocationError` stubbed in the test because commit 2 doesn't export it. "confirms a revoked project extension stopped by its process, retrying the reload once before giving up" reports `confirmed` for inventories that never confirm the pid stopped. "restarts an idle session…" and "restarts a busy session… only after its turn ends" time out waiting for a restart. "stops a session and fails its initialization when it can't confirm a revocation, before or after it registers" fails as well.
- **Commit 4:** the three new rows of "confirms a revoked project extension stopped by its process, retrying the reload once before giving up" fail on commit 3's code. A revoked extension listed with an unknown status before the reload gets no reload. One listed with an unknown status or an unknown source after a failed reload is reported `confirmed` after one reload.

**Code OSS verification** (dev build of the tip, macOS arm64, Agents window, local Copilot agent host against a mock LLM, Workspace Trust enabled), run with the `validate-ui-scenario` runner and checked against the agent host log. Each project canvas extension appends its pid to a launch log, so launches are counted independently of the UI. The "before" runs use the same scenario on the code without the fix.

| Scenario | After (tip) | Before |
|---|---|---|
| **Gap 1.** Two trusted folders. The consumer's `.github/extensions/supplied-canvas` links to a module in the supplier folder. The supplier's chat launches nothing, and the consumer's chat launches it once. Delete the supplier's chat: the extension keeps running, as it should. Then remove the supplier folder's trust. | passed: the pid exits within 15 seconds, nothing relaunches, and the log names only `supplied-canvas` ([video](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/main/vscode/canvas-trust-revocation-gaps/borrowed-after-add2e80acab.mp4)) | `main`: the pid is still alive 15 seconds later ([video](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/main/vscode/canvas-trust-revocation-gaps/borrowed-before.mp4)) |
| **Gap 2.** A quick chat with no workspace. A module in its scratch folder is linked from a trusted consumer folder, whose chat launches it once from the exempt scratch folder. Delete the quick chat. Workspace trust doesn't change. | passed: the pid exits within 15 seconds and nothing relaunches. The log reads "Reloading extensions after workspace trust was revoked for borrowed-canvas" ([video](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/main/vscode/canvas-trust-revocation-gaps/exemption-after-add2e80acab.mp4)) | commit 1: the pid is still alive 15 seconds later ([video](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/main/vscode/canvas-trust-revocation-gaps/exemption-before.mp4)) |

Gap 3 and commit 4 can't be driven from the UI. Gap 3 needs a reload that fails, or an inventory that still lists a revoked pid, and the UI can't inject either fault. Commit 4 needs a runtime that lists a source or status this host doesn't know, and the bundled runtime doesn't. The `CopilotAgent` tests above cover both.

**Regression check:** #343771's Code OSS scenarios, rerun on the tip, all pass: the trusted-folder gate with cold resume, two folders with targeted revocation, the open canvas tab, a new worktree inheriting trust, the no-workspace chats (with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, as in #343771), and the prewarmed draft. The worktree scenario needed a harness fix. The isolation menu's "New Worktree" row re-renders while it opens, so the click lost its target on both the tip and `main`. The scenario now retries the click and reopens the menu if it closed. Its assertions are unchanged. The variant of the no-workspace scenario without `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` fails at the same step on the tip and on `main`: the second chat's extension never launches, because the isolated home folder sits inside a git checkout (#343771's Known limitations). In the agent host logs of all these runs, no extension row has an unsupported source or status, and no revocation goes unconfirmed.

**CI pipeline:** Azure build 503988 of the VS Code (CI) pipeline passed on the tip: Quality Checks and every Windows x64, Linux x64 and macOS ARM64 job, including Agent Host E2E Tests (Electron) on all three. The PR's GitHub checks pass.

## Known limitations

- **A teardown that fails or hangs is not escalated.** When a revocation can't be confirmed, this PR restarts the session, and that relies on disconnecting it. If the disconnect fails, the extension may keep running. If it hangs, it also blocks the chat's queue, because `CopilotSessionWrapper.disconnect()` has no timeout (that part predates this PR). A chat that starts or resumes while its folder loses trust is blocked the same way, because its initialization waits for that disconnect before it fails. Separately, a canvas teardown that fails for another reason can leave extensions in a runtime the host no longer tracks. #350420 handles both: a teardown deadline, then stopping the runtime the session ran on. It's left out of this PR for three reasons:
  - It changes `_destroyLiveSession`, which has twelve callers.
  - Stopping the shared runtime ends the session of every chat on it, and each resumes on its next message.
  - The failure it handles hasn't been observed. A successful disconnect stopped the extension's process in a probe.

  Milestone 2's rule that no session stays live in an untrusted folder may make it unnecessary.
- **A busy session waits for its turn.** A busy session that can't confirm the revocation keeps the extension until its turn ends, then restarts.
- **The log wording is reused.** An exemption ending logs the same "workspace trust was revoked" line as a real revocation.
- **#343771's other limitations are unchanged.** For example, revocation still reloads every session that runs a same-named extension.

Follow-ups for the Copilot SDK/runtime, which would simplify this host logic: include the session id and discovery root in launch requests, and confirm extension stops in the reload result. With a session id, commit 1's discovery-root bookkeeping wouldn't be needed.

## Follow-up PRs

- #350400, stacked on this PR, fixes findings from a review of this PR. It confirms a revocation when a failed reload leaves nothing running, caps the wait for a relaunch at one second after the first list, and localizes the error a chat shows when a revocation can't be confirmed.
- #350420, stacked on #350400, adds the teardown deadline and the runtime stop that the first Known limitation describes.
- #350416, against `main`, keeps a canvas closed when it's closed while its chat is parked. That bug predates this PR. This PR's idle restart parks canvases the same way, so that fix covers it too once both merge (inferred).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added test demonstrates the exact stopped-inventory state being rejected and the two reloads. The production error handler and restart call path establish the additional lifecycle cost. No timing measurements are claimed.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Redundant extensions.reload IPC plus avoidable session-disconnect and subsequent session-resume work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One redundant reload per affected session per reconciliation, followed by one avoidable session teardown/resume if both reload attempts reject. The global pass processes sessions concurrently; this is not a per-extension reload count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra runtime lifecycle work and increased latency on the next chat or canvas operation.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A rejected reload ended that reconciliation attempt; for an already live session the agent logged the error and left the warm session available. There was no second reload or trust-revocation-driven session restart.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After a reload rejects, confirmation cannot succeed if the original revoked extension had no PID or an unreadable row, even when the new complete inventory contains no active extensions. The code unnecessarily reloads again and can request a whole-session restart.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The newly added condition (reloaded || !hasUnidentified) at line 7515 rejects an otherwise complete, stopped inventory. The surrounding new two-attempt loop then repeats rpc.extensions.reload and throws CopilotProjectExtensionRevocationError after another rejection.
Findings.Title: Accept a complete stopped inventory before retrying the reload
Findings.Impact: A reload that reports failure after successfully stopping a PID-less starting extension causes an unnecessary second reload. If it reports failure again, an otherwise usable warm chat is disconnected and the next send/canvas operation pays SDK-session resume costs despite a complete inventory already proving there is nothing active to stop.
Findings.Evidence: hasUnidentified is set when a revoked starting extension lacks a PID (line 7482). If reload rejects but all extensions are now failed/absent, inventory.complete is true and stillRunning is empty, yet the added guard forbids returning. The new test explicitly captures this case: reloadFailedForOneStartingWithoutProcess lists revoked('starting') before reload and only revoked('failed') afterwards (copilotAgent.test.ts:13379), but expects two reloads and an unconfirmed outcome (13414). The agent handles that error by marking and disposing the session when idle (copilotAgent.ts:2788-2790, 2593-2601), or restarting it on the next send/control operation (9027, 9114-9123).
Findings.Recommendation: Before requiring a successful reload for unidentified old processes, accept a complete inventory that has no active extensions. Preserve the conservative retry/restart behavior when the inventory is incomplete or an active extension could still be the unidentified process.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The fixed poll count, per-call timeout, two attempts, Promise.all barrier, and initialization await are all directly traced. Actual runtime inventory latency and the prevalence of PID-less starting rows are unknown, but do not change the multiplicative wait.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full-inventory IPC round trips, inventory serialization/allocation, and time occupying the reconciliation/initialization critical path.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Up to ten serialized inventory calls per reload attempt, twenty across two attempts, per affected session. Sessions run concurrently via Promise.all, but the next global reconciliation pass waits for the slowest. Ten successful five-second responses, for example, require about fifty seconds per attempt; this is a code-derived example, not a measurement.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Amplified reconciliation and chat-initialization latency on slow runtimes, plus repeated full-inventory IPC work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A contraction listed the session's extensions once and awaited one reload; it did not poll inventories after the reload. A combined expansion could perform one additional list.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Revocation confirmation now polls the full extension inventory up to ten times sequentially per reload attempt, with a fresh control-plane RPC timeout for every poll. The second reload attempt can repeat the entire polling sequence.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added _settledRuntimeExtensions loop awaits _listRuntimeExtensions at line 7530 before checking poll >= PROJECT_EXTENSION_SETTLE_POLLS and sleeping 100ms. _stopRevokedProjectExtensions calls this new loop inside its two-attempt reload loop.
Findings.Title: Use an elapsed-time deadline for extension settling
Findings.Impact: When a same-named extension is still starting without a PID and the runtime is slow to answer inventories, this ostensibly brief settling wait can last tens of seconds or minutes, delaying trust reconciliation for other sessions and blocking a starting/resuming chat when the change occurs during initialization.
Findings.Evidence: PROJECT_EXTENSION_SETTLE_POLLS is 10 and the interval is 100ms (lines 722-724), but inventory RPC durations are not included in any elapsed-time budget. _listRuntimeExtensions invokes _awaitControlPlaneRpc('rpc.extensions.list', ...) at line 5553; each call has its own default 30,000ms timeout (lines 681, 2591, 9410-9420). Slow successful inventories that continue to show a revoked name as starting without a PID therefore incur ten RPC round trips per attempt, not a roughly one-second bound. copilotAgent.ts:2776-2794 awaits all sessions before its global trust Throttler can run the next pass; initialization also directly awaits this reconciliation at 11668/11692.
Findings.Recommendation: Start an elapsed-time settling deadline after the first inventory and bound subsequent waits by its remaining budget. Stop polling once that deadline expires and use the existing bounded retry/restart decision.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The newly awaited cleanup, its uncapped disconnect/shutdown race, and the per-chat sequencer are explicit in the traced code. Pending disconnect behavior is also modeled in copilotAgentSession.test.ts:7207-7233 and 7500-7522. The frequency of a runtime stalling during this failure path is not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: The pending session-disconnect IPC, initialization promise, and serialized chat queue slot.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay is unbounded for each affected chat when neither the disconnect response nor shutdown arrives; queueing further operations cannot make progress. Other chat keys can still run.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Potentially indefinite chat initialization latency and head-of-line blocking of subsequent chat operations.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The reconciliation error propagated to callers such as _resumeSessionOnce, which called agentSession.dispose() and rethrew. Wrapper disposal started disconnect as best-effort asynchronous cleanup, without keeping the initializing operation pending on that response.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A failed trust revocation during initialization now awaits _destroyLiveSession before propagating the initialization error, moving session disconnect onto the initializing chat's serialized critical path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added await this._destroyLiveSession(session, true) at line 11674 precedes throw error; the added post-registration branch at line 11699 does the same. Neither added await has a deadline or cancellation race.
Findings.Title: Bound revocation teardown before awaiting it during initialization
Findings.Impact: If a chat starts or resumes while trust contracts and the unhealthy runtime fails revocation and then stalls disconnect without emitting shutdown, initialization and all subsequent sends/control operations queued for that chat remain blocked, even after cancellation. A single affected chat is sufficient.
Findings.Evidence: _destroyLiveSession awaits chatSession.destroySession() (copilotAgent.ts:11619-11631); destroySession awaits _wrapper.disconnect() (copilotAgentSession.ts:8705-8717). CopilotSessionWrapper.disconnect races only the disconnect promise against session.shutdown, and _disconnect directly awaits session.disconnect() (copilotSessionWrapper.ts:144-186). If neither arrives, this wait never settles. _queueChat awaits its task inside SequencerByKey and its stall timer only logs (copilotAgent.ts:10609-10627). _resumeSessionOnce's catch/dispose at 11855-11857 cannot execute until the newly added await finishes.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep teardown ordered, but give this awaited teardown a deadline and escalate through shutdown of the owning runtime if disconnect does not settle; do not hold initialization and the chat queue indefinitely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create/resume a canvas-enabled chat and allow or refuse its project-extension launches.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Admission and SDK-session initialization precede use of the chat. Each project-extension launch must resolve its canonical module and discovery root before the launch provider permits the extension subprocess. Existing SDK initialization and sandbox preparation remain on the startup path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize admitted directories and, where applicable, scratch/worktree metadata using fs.realpath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D admission-root calls; scratch validation adds two parallel canonicalizations, or worktree validation three. These counts are unchanged by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same directory and exemption canonicalization calls already ran during admission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Admission must finish before session initialization proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the module path and newly resolve the folder above .github/extensions for project launch bookkeeping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing module realpath plus one new discovery-root realpath for each normally shaped project-extension launch request; no discovery-root call for other path shapes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the module canonicalization was awaited here; discovery-root canonicalization did not run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both results are awaited before the corresponding extension may launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to T distinct successful cold reads shared across launches; zero additional successful-root filesystem reads when warm. Unresolved roots may be retried on subsequent decisions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same successful/in-flight cache and retry-on-missing behavior existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Nonexempt trust decisions await these roots.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/resume an SDK session and answer runtime extension-launch requests; permitted extensions use the existing Node/bootstrap launch configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal SDK create/resume per chat initialization, with launch-provider callbacks for extensions the runtime starts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK launch and extension subprocess path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing startup and individual extension-launch dependencies; no new direct network request is introduced by this bookkeeping.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D admitted directories, E project-extension launch requests across sessions, and T distinct trusted URI strings. Launch records deduplicate by requested path plus canonical module; different sessions requesting the same path still perform launch-time canonicalization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Admission directory reads remain sequential. The module and discovery-root reads for one launch now run in Promise.all. Trusted URI reads run in parallel and share in-flight promises. Independent runtime launch requests are not globally limited here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful trusted-root promises are cached/coalesced per trusted URI and cleared on workspace-trust changes. Missing roots are removed and retried. Scratch exemptions bypass trusted-root reads. The module and newly introduced discovery-root realpaths are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: launch callback wiring, filesystem calls, cache ownership, and startup call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No filesystem timings or real-world extension counts are available. The added discovery-root canonicalization is bounded per launch and necessary for the new ownership tracking; no separate high-confidence regression is reported for it.
Scenarios.Verdict: Normal launch bookkeeping introduces one additional filesystem canonicalization per project launch, but no independently actionable performance regression was established on this normal path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a workspace-trust expansion or contraction to already live canvas sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The policy computes affected extension names before the agent lists live sessions. The global trust Throttler cannot advance to its next pass until Promise.all of the current canvas sessions settles. This normally runs outside send/control queues, except for reconciliation performed during initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recheck allowed launch trust using canonical trusted roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to T successful cold trusted-root realpaths shared across all N records; warm successes perform no filesystem read. Missing roots may be retried on later record checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Contractions already scanned allowed launches and checked the same cached trust roots; the diff retains some records longer to cover borrowed extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy reconciliation finishes before session RPC fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List extension inventories; reload affected sessions; confirm stops by additional inventories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial inventory per S session. Normal successful revocation adds one confirmation inventory per affected session and one grouped reload per K session. Failure/starting cases can perform two reloads and up to twenty confirmation inventories per affected session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One initial inventory per session and one reload per affected session, with at most an additional list for a combined expansion; no post-reload confirmation polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The slowest session holds the current global reconciliation pass. Additional confirmation calls are new.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime reload stops/restarts enabled extension providers, consulting the existing launch provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped once per affected session in the successful case, up to twice in the new retry path, not once per extension. Each reload can affect that session's other enabled providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One grouped reload was already used; the retry introduces a possible second provider lifecycle cycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reload completion is awaited before confirmation; provider readiness can continue afterwards.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconcile failed/refused project extensions after trust expands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one reconcile call for each of R sessions with failed project extensions in a pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same expansion retry already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the same per-pass Promise.all barrier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct recorded allowed launches, D distinct admitted roots, S live canvas-enabled sessions, K sessions with an active revoked extension or an incomplete inventory, and R sessions with failed project extensions after an expansion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Policy launch checks are awaited sequentially, with shared trusted-root promises. One global Throttler serializes passes and coalesces changes into at most one queued successor. Within a pass all S session reconciliations run concurrently; multiple revoked names in one session share a reload.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace-trust changes clear canonical trusted-root promises. Successful trusted roots are resolved at most once per URI per generation, not once per launch. Failed roots can be retried. Inventory snapshots are not cached between calls. Launch bookkeeping is pruned conservatively by discovery root.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: grouping is per session and the global/per-session ordering is directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session counts, provider startup costs, inventory sizes, and runtime RPC durations are not measured. The normal extra confirmation is intentional; the avoidable repeated-work cases are reported separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: The confirmation design intentionally adds bounded normal work. Reported issues concern its wall-clock-unbounded polling budget and unnecessary retry/restart when a complete inventory already shows everything stopped.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or close a scratch/worktree exemption that another chat's extension borrows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Admission acquisition/release updates reference counts and scans recorded launches synchronously; relevant exemption changes schedule background reconciliation. The policy's trust counters also make initializing sessions catch up before returning to their caller.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve admitted scratch/worktree roots and their repository relationships.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same admission and scratch/worktree canonicalization counts as before; no filesystem work is added by the synchronous event emission itself.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canonicalization and reference counting already occurred, but did not schedule reconciliation for exemptions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule existing inventory/reload/reconcile RPCs when an exemption changes under a recorded launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced pass serving accumulated changes; one initial list per eligible live canvas session when affected names/expansion remain, then grouped operations only for relevant sessions. No inventory RPC if pruning produces no affected names and there is no expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exemption changes alone did not schedule these runtime operations, leaving borrowed extensions unreconciled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normally background; initializing sessions separately catch up on their startup path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to two exemption roots changed by an admission, N recorded allowed/refused launches keyed by requested/canonical path, and S live canvas sessions. A supplier closing with no remaining chat under a discovery root allows pruning before any session RPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Change events reuse the global Throttler, OR accumulated expansion/contraction flags, and coalesce changes arriving during a running pass. Session RPCs within the resulting pass run concurrently, not under a global per-session limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exemption changes advance the trust generation without clearing successful canonical workspace-trust roots. Shared exemptions use reference counts, so only first admission/last release can signal a change. Refused records are removed after success or pruned on reconciliation; unknown discovery roots remain conservatively retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event gating, reference counts, pruning, and coalescing are explicit in source and new policy tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Borrowed scratch/worktree extensions are specialized; launch-history sizes are unknown. No large retained-object graph or avoidable boundary burst was established beyond the separately reported retry behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: New reconciliation is required for the intended lifecycle semantics and is coalesced. No additional finding for exemption events or conservative launch retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Confirm revocation while a same-named provider remains starting without a PID and inventory reads are slow.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each reload attempt awaits the settling loop; the global pass and any initialization-time reconciliation await that loop. Ordinary sends are not universally blocked by the background pass, but newly initializing/resuming chats that are catching up are.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeatedly fetch and decode the complete extension inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to ten successful list calls per attempt, twenty across retries, per affected session, plus its initial pre-reload list. A timed-out list aborts that attempt rather than being repeated ten times within it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No contraction-only post-reload polling existed; combined expansion could list once more.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Successful slow calls can stretch the nominal short settle period to tens of seconds or minutes and delay the pass/initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive and map each complete inventory, including PID/status normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Linear in inventory rows for every issued poll; no per-row IPC fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inventory decoding existed, but did not repeat through this new polling loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of each awaited inventory operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K affected sessions, each potentially making ten successful inventory RPCs per attempt and two attempts; each response's duration adds serially within its session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Polls are sequential per session with 100ms sleeps. A new 30-second RPC timeout starts for every call. K sessions can poll concurrently, while the global trust Throttler waits for the slowest.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every poll makes a fresh full inventory RPC. Trusted-root caching does not coalesce or shorten inventory polling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High and independent of magnitude: call count, serial waits, individual timeout, and critical-path callers are directly proven.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No observed inventory latency distribution is available; slow successful replies are the trigger, not ten consecutive timeouts. Numeric examples in the finding are explicitly derived rather than measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: use an elapsed-time deadline instead of treating ten individually timed RPCs as a short settling bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: A reload rejects after stopping a PID-less extension, versus a genuinely unconfirmed revocation requiring idle/busy-session fallback.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a failed confirmation the agent marks restart required. Idle teardown runs through the chat sequencer; busy sessions wait for their own turn/subagents to finish, or restart before a subsequent send/control operation. The next use of a disposed session must resume it before proceeding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry extensions.reload and list again despite a complete inventory with only failed/absent extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One avoidable second reload and another confirmation sequence per affected session; two rejected reloads trigger the restart fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A rejected reload ended reconciliation with a logged failure for live sessions, without a second reload or trust-specific restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds work before the pass finishes and may unnecessarily invalidate the warm chat session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush/release session state and disconnect the SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disconnect per retiring wrapper, shared across concurrent disconnect requests; pre-disconnect sampling-interest release is one existing bounded RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A non-timeout reload rejection alone did not schedule this trust-specific live-session teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occupies the chat queue until teardown completes. This is intended for genuine unconfirmed revocations, avoidable for the stopped-inventory case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read stored session metadata and customization state to rebuild the resumed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing resume-path reads once per subsequent cold resume; newly reached when this false-negative confirmation disposes a previously warm session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The already live session could be reused after a non-timeout reload failure; no forced cold-resume reads were required by this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The next send or canvas/control operation waits for restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the SDK session and perform its existing registration/control-plane setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resume plus the normal initialization RPCs per replacement wrapper; enabled extension providers can relaunch through the normal launch path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These boundaries existed for ordinary cold resume, but were not reached solely because this stopped-inventory reload had rejected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the next operation can use a disposed chat's runtime.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected sessions, not extension names: at most two reload attempts per session, one coalesced wrapper disconnect, and one later SDK-session resume when used again.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The global pass handles independent sessions concurrently. Teardown and subsequent work are serialized per chat. Wrapper disconnect requests share _disconnectPromise; there is no per-extension disconnect fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A complete inventory is authoritative but the new hasUnidentified gate prevents using even an entirely inactive inventory after a failed reload. Disposing drops the warm SDK wrapper; retained metadata/customization anchors do not eliminate the later SDK resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the new table test explicitly expects two reloads and failure for starting-without-PID followed by failed-only inventory; production handling traces directly to disposal/resume.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real reload-rejection rates and resume costs are unknown. The finding is limited to complete inactive inventories and does not object to restarting when a process could still run.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: accept a complete inventory with no active extensions before retrying or forcing session restart.

Scenarios.Scenario: Trust contracts while a chat initializes or resumes, reconciliation fails, and teardown does not return a response or shutdown event.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initialization already holds the chat queue. The added error branches now await _destroyLiveSession before propagating failure; the caller's dispose/rethrow and queue release cannot occur first. This wait has no cancellation/deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await SDK-session disconnect after initialization-time revocation failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared disconnect operation per wrapper. Neither repeated calls nor cancellation create a completion deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For a failure during initialization, the error reached the caller's dispose/rethrow; wrapper disposal initiated best-effort disconnect without waiting for it before the operation failed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly moves potentially nonterminating disconnect onto initialization and the chat's serialized critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release sampling-event interest before session disconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing releaseInterest RPC per wrapper, bounded by the control-plane timeout, after pending output captures settle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cleanup occurred during wrapper teardown, but initialization failure did not await that best-effort disposal path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing disconnect preparation now also lies in the added awaited initialization cleanup; unlike the final disconnect RPC, this individual interest-release RPC is bounded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One affected initialization suffices. Further operations on that chat accumulate behind its sequencer; independent chat keys can progress.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One chat sequencer slot is held through cleanup. CopilotSessionWrapper waits on either disconnect response or shutdown. The chat stall timer only logs and does not release the task.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Coalesced default/peer resume promises remain pending until initialization completes. Disconnect calls share one promise, which avoids duplicate IPC but supplies no time bound; ordinary caches cannot release the queue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added awaited cleanup, caller disposal catch, promise races, queue ordering, and logging-only stall warning are established in code. Existing tests explicitly model pending disconnects and shutdown as the alternative completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No production rate for a stalled runtime failing both revocation and teardown is established. The indefinite queue-blocking mechanism is distinct from that prevalence uncertainty.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: preserve teardown ordering but bound it and escalate through the owning runtime rather than wedging chat initialization indefinitely.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages against base beaa31d361bfe0fc386285370819b343941a9c0c. Submitted three high-confidence findings: newly awaited unbounded initialization teardown, poll-count rather than elapsed-time settling, and redundant retry/session restart despite a complete stopped inventory. Traced startup, trust changes, exemption changes, polling, fallback restart, caches, grouping, and per-chat/global sequencing. No separate findings for necessary discovery-root I/O, conservative launch records, metadata projection, or intentional fail-closed handling. Investigated provenance of retained borrowed-extension processes, but did not record a performance-regression fix because blame of the trust-policy change alone does not establish a prior performance worsening.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
